page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-16 is a memory-oriented virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, accompanied by standard AVX, BMI2, and FMA extensions, though advanced AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets are unsupported.

The configuration provides 128 GB of system memory, delivering a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio (8 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage and possesses no hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage options for persistent disk requirements. In benchmark testing, uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 72.07 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 45.47 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput in-memory data processing.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core stress performance, placing within the top 25 percent of tested systems with a score of 2690.19 in stress-ng. Multi-core operations register in the middle tier, yielding a multi-core stress-ng score of 21569.57, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9397, and a PassMark CPU rating of 21848.92. In data operations, the instance handles 16.05 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database rating of 6646.26, while static web serving throughput measures 15.13 GB/sec.

Given its elevated RAM capacity per core paired with mid-tier multi-threaded compute density, the n2d-highmem-16 offers solid cost efficiency for memory-bound applications without necessitating specialized enterprise memory pricing. It represents a practical tradeoff for workloads that depend heavily on large memory footprints rather than extreme compute parallelism. The instance is well suited for in-memory caching tiers, relational database engines, memory-intensive CI/CD build environments, and enterprise ETL pipelines.

It provides 128 GB of system RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, while omitting local storage and hardware GPUs. The processor includes standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI acceleration extensions. Benchmarks reflect strong single-core stress execution alongside balanced multi-core output, yielding 21569.57 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 72.07 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth, and 16.05 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance delivers favorable cost efficiency for memory-bound systems that do not need top-tier compute density. The platform is well aligned for mid-sized relational databases, distributed caching layers, big data preprocessing, and ETL operations.
